summary: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5 (a broadly available Mythos-class model) and Claude Mythos 5 (a less-restricted version for trusted cyber-defense and biology partners), with new safety classifiers, a 30-day data retention policy, and pricing at $10/$50 per million input/output tokens.

mechanisms.reason: The lab states the new model exceeds all previously released models and is state-of-the-art on nearly all benchmarks, including long-horizon agentic tasks.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5\u2019s capabilities exceed those of any model we\u2019ve ever made generally available. It is state-of-the-art on nearly all tested benchmarks of AI capability

mechanisms.reason: The new frontier-class model is priced at less than half the cost of its predecessor tier, lowering per-token economics for a top-of-range model.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 are being offered at $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens\u2014less than half the price of Claude Mythos Preview.

mechanisms.reason: Longer autonomous operation and multi-agent workflows described by customers imply substantially more tokens consumed per task.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 and Mythos 5 can work autonomously for longer than any previous Claude models.

mechanisms.reason: The model is described as maintaining focus and using persistent notes across millions of tokens, increasing context and memory demands per query.
mechanisms.quote: Fable 5 stays focused across millions of tokens in long-running tasks and improves its outputs using its own notes.

mechanisms.reason: Customer testimony describes the model autonomously completing large-scale engineering work that previously required teams of humans, illustrating displacement of manual/seat-based labor by agentic execution.
mechanisms.quote: In a 50-million-line Ruby codebase, the model performed a codebase-wide migration in a day that would otherwise have taken a whole team over two months by hand.

notable_reason: This is a major frontier model launch from Anthropic with disclosed capability jumps, a price cut versus the prior tier, and new agentic/cyber-capability safeguards, which is directly relevant to anyone tracking frontier AI economics.
